messages:
emma.support: Hey team — customer on Dedicated reported an incident where their payment provider webhook was executed twice after our function-call retry. They got an HTTP 202 from the tool and then we retried, which caused the provider to charge twice. Customer is asking for a refund and a root cause.
sam.engineering: Ugh. Do we have the thread/logs? 202 usually means accepted — should we treat it as terminal for tool invocations.
emma.support: Pasting relevant excerpt from the customer's agent logs (sanitized):
```
REQUEST: POST /v1/call_tool
Headers: {"Authorization":"Bearer <short-lived>", "Idempotency-Key": null}
Payload: {"tool":"payment_webhook","args":{...}}
RESPONSE (tool): 202 Accepted
-- client sees 202, then our SDK retries after auth refresh --
REQUEST RETRY (new token): POST /v1/call_tool
Headers: {"Authorization":"Bearer <refreshed>", "Idempotency-Key": null}
RESPONSE (tool): 200 OK -> webhook executed again
```
emma.support: Customer says timestamps: first exec 202 @2023-11-15T18:12:03Z, second exec 200 @18:12:07Z. They billed two charges.
lee.platform: Thanks. Looks like two root causes: (1) our retry logic treated 202 as transient instead of accepted, (2) idempotency key was missing so the payment endpoint had no dedupe.
maria.billing: Customer is requesting immediate refund for the duplicate charge. I can process it but need a confirmation + internal note. Any immediate mitigation we should recommend to them? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sam.engineering: Short-term: tell them to include an Idempotency-Key in the tool args/header until we patch. Long-term: change retry policy so that 202 from known external tool endpoints is treated as success for invocation semantics. Also consider adding automatic idempotency-key generation in our SDK for tool calls.
emma.support: I've told the customer to set an Idempotency-Key and held the refund pending internal confirmation. They responded that they rely on our SDK for auth refresh and didn't expect a second call.
sam.engineering: Can repro locally. Steps I ran:
1) start local mock tool that returns 202 for first request, 200 for subsequent.
2) call our client with expired token -> trigger refresh during call.
3) observe retry path invoking tool again.
Logs:
```
[t=00:00:00] client -> runtime: POST /invoke tool=payment_webhook
[t=00:00:01] runtime -> tool: 202 Accepted
[t=00:00:02] client -> auth: refresh token (401 on kv)
[t=00:00:03] client -> runtime: RETRY POST /invoke tool=payment_webhook
[t=00:00:04] runtime -> tool: 200 OK (webhook fired)
```
sam.engineering: The retry is happening because the client call path didn't correlate the original '202' as a completed tool execution when auth refresh happened concurrently.
lee.platform: Quick mitigation we can deploy: change the runtime to treat '202 Accepted' as an authoritative terminal state for tool invocations coming from external webhooks when the tool declares 'acceptance' semantics. I'll file a small config flag plus a patch to the retry classifier. Can we push a canary to Dedicated tomorrow? @ops-bot can you schedule? :spiral_calendar_pad:
ops-bot: Scheduled canary deploy to dedicated-us-west tomorrow 02:00 UTC. Will run for 30m and route 1% traffic. Logs will be sent to #eng-sre-canary.
maria.billing: I'll start the refund flow for the customer and add a note referencing this thread. Please confirm the customer will get a rollback once we patch.
sam.engineering: We'll also add a validation at SDK-level to warn when Idempotency-Key is absent for tool calls whose tool type is in a configured 'side-effecting' category (payments, provisioning, outbound webhooks). That should prevent accidental double-exec for new integrations.
emma.support: Customer asked for an interim webhook replay detector. Any chance we can add a simple dedupe window on the provider-facing requests? Even a short TTL with 'Idempotency-Key' if present.
lee.platform: Good idea — runtime can set an internal-generated Idempotency-Key when none provided and persist it in the call record for 10s to dedupe immediate retries. We'll include that in the canary.
sam.engineering: I'll open PR with the retry classifier change + SDK warning + internal idempotency header injector. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/PR-2412 (will add more details).
emma.support: I'll ping the customer with the refund confirmation and the planned canary. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
